title: Vayelech: strong and of good courage (Deuteronomy 31:7)
hookLine: Moses encourages Joshua in front of all Israel

lines: OR: OUT LOUD, IN FRONT OF EVERYONE.
cards: A text before an interview. A hand on the shoulder in a hallway. A quiet good luck at the door.
Private encouragement is real, and good. But there's another kind that's harder to give: saying it out loud, in front of everyone, so the person hears it and so does everyone around them.
It puts the speaker's own name behind someone else. Moses chooses that kind.

teach.h: IN THE SIGHT OF ALL ISRAEL.
teach.b: "And Moses called unto Joshua, and said unto him in the sight of all Israel: 'Be strong and of good courage.'" In Hebrew, chazak ve'ematz. Two words that overlap: be strong, be firm.
Moses had already said the same words to the whole people a few verses earlier. Now he says them to one man, in front of everyone. Consider Joshua's position.

He's following Moses, the one who spoke with God. Someone in his place might well wonder whether he could measure up, and whether the people would follow. A public blessing answers both doubts at once.
Joshua hears that his teacher believes in him. And the people hear it too, so they know their new leader didn't grab the role. It was handed to him, with confidence, in daylight.
The words keep traveling. Later in this chapter God says them to Joshua directly, and again, more than once, at the opening of the book of Joshua. And they've entered Jewish life in another form.
In Ashkenazi synagogues, when the reading of one of the five books of the Torah is finished, the congregation calls out: chazak, chazak, venitchazek.
Be strong, be strong, and let us be strengthened.
When Deuteronomy ends, in two weeks on our path, it will be said again.
Courage, in this verse, isn't something Joshua has to find alone. It's given to him, out loud, by the teacher he has served since the early days in the wilderness.

how: When the reading of each of the five books of the Torah is completed, Ashkenazi congregations call out 'chazak, chazak, venitchazek', be strong, be strong, and let us be strengthened; other communities have their own words for the moment.

games.q: you're handing your role to Joshua, and the people aren't sure about him. what does Moses do?
o: warn Joshua privately about his weaknesses.
encourage him in front of all Israel.
games.why: a public charge: Joshua hears his teacher's confidence, and the people hear that the role was given, not taken.

practice: Think of someone stepping into something new or hard, a colleague in a new role, a kid trying out for something, a friend starting over, and find one true sentence you believe about them.
Picture saying it where others can hear it, at the dinner table or in the group chat: not flattery, just the true thing, with your name behind it.
